papers.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
papers.summary: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. We present CALOMERA, a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population synthesis framework in which the vertical density profiles of mono-age subpopulations are computed self-consistently with the Galactic potential and coupled to modern WD cooling sequences, metallicity-dependent progenitor lifetimes and synthetic photometry. We calibrate 18 parameters describing the initial mass function, SFH, initial-final mass relation and WD population against a Gaia DR3 sample of $7.98\times10^{6}$ stars within 1 kpc, including $1.1\times10^{5}$ WDs. The calibrated model reproduces the star counts in each colour-magnitude diagram region to within 3% and the total number count to within 0.5%, compared with the 81% excess in the predicted WD count obtained with the previous main-sequence-only calibration. The recovered SFH peaks early, declines exponentially thereafter, and includes two recent bursts, located at $τ\approx2.4$ and $0.5$ Gyr. Three cooling libraries (Montréal, BaSTI and LPCODE) yield comparably good fits, with differences confined to ${\rm M_G}\gtrsim15$ mag. The predicted luminosity function is in reasonable agreement with the 100 pc Gaia WD sample. We further predict the Galactic WD distribution and differential number counts for surveys of varying depth. Extending the framework to the substellar regime using ATMO models, we predict the Galactic L, T, and Y dwarf populations and their contribution to the deep JWST fields.
papers.comment: Submitted to MNRAS, 20 pages main text + 4 pages appendix, 13 figures

papers.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
papers.summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
papers.summary: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
papers.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

papers.title: Decoupling Dynamics: A Tale of Two Limits
papers.summary: The symmetries of a $d$-dimensional QFT are known to be captured by a topological theory in one dimension higher, the Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which is invariant under gauging finite symmetries of the QFT, but not under dynamical gauging of continuous symmetries. We show that the distinct SymTFTs of a $d$-dimensional QFT before and after dynamical gauging of a continuous Abelian symmetry arise as different topological limits of the same dynamical holographic gauge theory in $(d+1)$-dimensions. Gauging changes the boundary condition of this dynamical theory and thereby selects a different topological limit, explaining why the associated SymTFT changes. We give a fully quantum definition of these SymTFTs at the level of Hilbert spaces and operators by combining suitable limits of the bulk holographic theory with photon truncation. This construction clarifies how topological symmetry defects, charges, and anomalies survive while the dynamical information carried by currents is discarded. We study non-anomalous and anomalous examples, providing a complete quantum analysis for $(2+1)$-dimensional bulks. For a four-dimensional boundary theory with a mixed axial-vector anomaly, we recover the SymTFT of the non-invertible chiral symmetry that remains after gauging the vector symmetry.
category_names_zh: hep-th (高能物理 - 理论 (场论/弦论))

papers.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
papers.summary: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.
category_names_zh: hep-th (高能物理 - 理论 (场论/弦论))

papers.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
papers.summary: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition. For Haar-random circuits, the TE transitions from a trivial identity ensemble to the uniform Haar ensemble, while the PE transitions from the Haar ensemble to a trivial singleton pure state. In Clifford circuits, absence of non-stabiliserness limits the PE to a $1$-design, while the TE forms a $k$-design for $k \leq 3$. We demonstrate that these genuine ensemble transitions offer a clear physical mechanism for the measurement-induced entanglement or purification transitions, illustrating how the capacity to ergodically steer a quantum subsystem shifts from the temporal boundary measurements in the mixed phase to the bulk trajectory measurements in the pure phase.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
papers.summary: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.
category_names_zh: hep-th (高能物理 - 理论 (场论/弦论))

papers.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
papers.summary: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
papers.summary: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: Euclid data release 1 (DR1) - SIR spectroscopic calibration
papers.summary: The Euclid space mission is dedicated to probing the nature of dark energy and dark matter, through a comprehensive mapping of the Universe's large-scale structure. Central to these cosmological goals are the spectra produced by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) and reduced by the scientific pipelines of the SIR (Spectral near InfraRed) processing function. Due to the intrinsic complexity of slitless spectroscopic data, scientific observations cannot be self-calibrated by the science pipelines. Consequently, the development of dedicated SIR calibration pipelines, utilising specific pointing sequences and observation fields, is essential. The resulting calibration products are fundamental to ensuring that reduced spectra are characterised within requirements in both wavelength and flux. This paper provides a detailed description of the SIR calibration pipelines responsible for generating the products utilised by the science pipelines for Data Release 1 (DR1). A significant challenge in these calibration tasks arises from the requirement to model the entire focal plane as a unified entity. Such a global modelling approach is critical for maintaining astrometric and spectroscopic continuity across the entire field of view. DR1 provides more than 170 millions validated spectra in both red- and blue-grism modes. The accuracy of the reduced spectra is strictly dependent on the performance of the calibration pipelines. Comprehensive analyses of the calibration products and the resulting science spectra demonstrate that current outputs successfully meet the mission requirements. Nevertheless, specific areas for optimisation have been identified; ongoing development is focused on addressing these critical points to further enhance data quality for future data releases.
category_names_zh: astro-ph.CO (宇宙学与河外天体物理)
papers.comment: 13 pages, 13 figures, submitted for publication to A&A

papers.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
papers.summary: The JWST Rocky Worlds Director's Discretionary Time (RWDDT) program uses secondary eclipse observations to determine the conditions under which rocky exoplanets around M dwarfs retain their atmospheres. We present RWDDT MIRI/F1500W observations of LTT 1445 A b and c, the transiting rocky siblings in the nearest such system (6.9 pc), comprising two eclipses of each planet across three visits. We perform three independent reductions and a joint fit that includes all existing JWST data and 220 radial velocities, improving the precision on the planetary radii, masses, and orbital parameters by factors of 1.6-2.3. We measure eclipse depths of $157^{+18}_{-17}$ ppm and $154^{+54}_{-37}$ ppm for planets b and c, corresponding to 15 $μ$m brightness temperatures of $528^{+39}_{-29}$ K and $625^{+109}_{-79}$ K, both consistent with the dark, bare rock limit. For planet b, combining these data with the archival MIRI/LRS spectrum in a Bayesian retrieval limits the CO$_2$ partial pressure to $<0.6$ mbar and the surface pressure to $\lesssim0.1$ bar, while forward models exclude thick aerosol layers that could mimic a bare surface in transmission. We conclude that planet b has no substantial atmosphere. For planet c, a potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave the depth poorly constrained; the data rule out only thick, CO$_2$-bearing atmospheres ($\gtrsim1$ bar with $\geq1\%$ CO$_2$). LTT 1445 A b is the planet closest to the canonical XUV-driven Cosmic Shoreline observed in eclipse so far. Its lack of a substantial atmosphere implies that the Cosmic Shoreline cannot lie much farther toward the airless side than nominally predicted.
papers.comment: Submitted to AAS Journals, comments welcome

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.summary: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

papers.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
papers.summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
papers.summary: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

papers.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
papers.summary: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
papers.summary: Ceramic materials that maintain structural integrity and resist thermal-shock under extreme conditions are critical for many applications. Here we show that spark plasma sintered composites containing equal weight fractions of hexagonal silicon carbide (6H-SiC) and boron nitride (h-BN) exhibit exceptional stability under extreme high-temperature oxidizing conditions and unusually stable temperature-independent thermal conductivity across a broad temperature range. Under high-velocity oxygen-fuel torch exposure in air, it withstands prolonged heating and thermal-cycling at surface temperatures reaching >1500 °C, whereas pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractures or erodes. Microstructural evaluation shows the formation of a multi-phase surface silica layer that further protects the material from oxidation. Finite-element analysis heat-flux map shows that intrinsic porosity mitigates thermal stress, while ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations reveal thermally driven interfacial reconstruction and the formation of a Si-N/C-B-rich bonding network, enhancing the interfacial cohesion at elevated temperatures. This lightweight, easily machinable ceramic composite will be a promising structural material in extreme environment applications.
papers.comment: 76 Pages, 4 Main Figures, 30 SI Figures, 8 Tables, Authors version, Comments are welcome

papers.title: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
papers.summary: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
papers.summary: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.

papers.title: On stimulated scattering including harmonic generation in an unmagnetized pair plasma for arbitrary pump strengths
papers.summary: A fully nonlinear analysis for the growth rate of the stimulated backscatter instability of an intense electromagnetic (EM) wave with arbitrary polarization in an unmagnetized pair plasma is presented. The connection of this instability to the FEL process is discussed and utilized. An intense EM wave causes an initially stationary pair plasma to drift forward with a speed near the speed of light. The resulting distribution function for both cold and warm pair plasmas is presented. It is shown that the frequency of the reflected light is thus Doppler downshifted from that of the incident wave. For a linearly polarized EM wave there is also an additional contribution to the forward drift at its second harmonic which leads to backscattered light at all odd harmonics of the Doppler downshifted frequency for sufficiently cold pair plasmas. Fully nonlinear particle-in-cell simulations confirm the theoretical growth rates and show how the instability depends on the pair plasma temperature. The effect of the intensity profile of the incoming EM wave as well as implications for astrophysical pair plasmas is discussed.

papers.title: Active-space construction in single-fragment coupled-cluster embedding for chemical reactions
papers.summary: We benchmark single-fragment quantum embedding, in which electron correlation---at the level of coupled-cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]---is restricted to orbitals associated with a chosen molecular fragment, and the remaining orbitals are frozen at the Hartree-Fock level. We compare several methods for constructing fragment active spaces, and we test their performance on 60 organic reaction energies and three reaction profiles. A common fragment projection operator is used to relate several of the tested orbital constructions. Regional embedding, based on density matrix embedding theory, is shown to give accurate and robust performance when used for both the occupied and virtual active orbitals. For virtual orbitals, fragment-centered projected atomic orbitals and fragment natural orbitals (defined by eigenvectors of a fragment MP2 density matrix) also perform well, but the latter typically retains larger virtual spaces. Composite MP2 corrections yield the largest improvement: combined with fragment natural orbitals, they give average reaction energy errors below 0.3 kcal/mol relative to full-system CCSD(T), with all individual errors below 1 kcal/mol. Reaction profiles show that accurate endpoint energies can conceal substantial barrier errors, emphasizing the importance of approximating omitted correlation.

papers.title: The $(5,5)$ String
papers.summary: We study an $N=(2,1)$ heterotic string with right-movers on $\mathbb R^{2,2}$ and left-movers of signature $(5,5)$, obtained by adjoining the lattice $\mathrm{II}_{3,3}$. Unlike the standard $N=(2,1)$ strings it requires no null current, and its target space remains four-dimensional. All of its states, an infinite tower with sixteen supercharges, are massless. For the neutral bosons, the Kutasov-Martinec determinant action is dual to a cubic action for a self-dual metric coupled to self-dual Maxwell fields, and we complete it with fermions using a single superfield. For the charged states we give evidence that the couplings are the structure constants of a Lie superalgebra formed by the physical states of the left-movers. We are thus led to propose that the classical target theory is a self-dual gauge theory for this superalgebra: every state of the string is a gauge field, and gravity is part of the gauge algebra. This would be a purely cubic field theory of all the modes of a closed string.
category_names_zh: hep-th (高能物理 - 理论 (场论/弦论))

papers.title: A precision bound for gravitational transseries
papers.summary: We propose that the large $N$ transseries of a holographic observable above the black hole threshold admits a precision bound, a limit on how precisely the transseries can determine the observable at finite $N$, set by the data of its D-brane instanton sectors. In doing so, we develop methods in large $N$ resurgence, based on the work of Écalle, that capture the $e^{-N^2}$ asymptotics of gravitational saddles beyond the $e^{-N}$ instantons. Under an assumption on the growth of the D-brane instanton sums that we expect in the black hole phase, we find an analytic obstruction to the resummation of the large $N$ transseries. This obstruction sets the precision bound. As our main example and consistency check, we study the $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills and its black hole. We derive relations between the D-brane instanton data on thermal AdS and on the black hole, in the form of a duality that exchanges the numbers of D-brane instantons on the two backgrounds. In the index, these relations reproduce the actions of D3-branes wrapped on the black hole. We conclude with our expectations for generic situations and their relation to the double-cone wormhole.
category_names_zh: hep-th (高能物理 - 理论 (场论/弦论))

papers.title: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks
papers.summary: We investigate boundary-induced stiffness in discrete-time quantum walks confined to a finite lattice by unitary reflecting boundaries implemented through coin-flip operations. We define a dimensionless spreading stiffness from the instantaneous variation of the spatial width relative to the asymptotic spreading rate of the corresponding unconfined Hadamard walk and compare localized, Gaussian, and truncated-uniform initial states. The long-time response retains a strong dependence on the initial spatial profile: the localized and truncated-uniform states show an overall increase in stiffness with increasing confinement size, whereas the Gaussian state exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence with a broad maximum at intermediate sizes. The first and second stiffness moments satisfy the expected asymptotic consistency relation in the high-stiffness regime. The normalized Kullback--Leibler divergence reveals a slower spatial reorganization and qualitatively different finite-size trends, showing that dynamical stiffness and spatial homogenization are distinct properties. These results indicate that unitary confinement produces an intrinsically nonstationary regime whose long-time properties emerge from the interplay between boundary reflections, system size, and the spatial structure of the initial state.
category_names_zh: quant-ph (量子力学、量子通信与量子计算)

papers.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
papers.summary: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.
